hints: Focus on what has to break during alkaline hydrolysis, the carbon to halogen bond attacked by $\text{OH}^-$ in nucleophilic substitution.
Compare the $\text{C-Cl}$ bond with the $\text{C-I}$ bond for strength, remembering that bond strength falls down Group 17.
Link a stronger, harder to break bond to the need for more vigorous heating to get the reaction done in a reasonable time.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the reaction needs**

Think of this as nucleophilic substitution. The $\text{OH}^-$ must break the $\text{C-X}$ bond to form $\text{C-OH}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{X} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{X}^-$$

**Compare C-I with C-Cl**

Reactivity of halogenoalkanes is controlled mainly by bond enthalpy, not polarity. Iodine is larger, so the $\text{C-I}$ bond is longer and weaker and breaks easily with gentle warming.

Bond strength order: $\text{C-F} > \text{C-Cl} > \text{C-Br} > \text{C-I}$

**Choose harsher conditions for the chloroalkane**

Because the $\text{C-Cl}$ bond is stronger than the $\text{C-I}$ bond, it needs more energy to break. So gentle warming is not enough, you must heat under reflux for a longer, hotter reaction without losing volatile reactants.

options.A: Heat under reflux is the right condition, but the reason is wrong. The $\text{C-Cl}$ bond is indeed more polar than $\text{C-I}$, but greater polarity would make attack by $\text{OH}^-$ easier, not harder. Reactivity here is decided by bond strength.
options.B: Correct. The $\text{C-Cl}$ bond is stronger (higher bond enthalpy) than the $\text{C-I}$ bond, so it is harder to break. More vigorous heating, heat under reflux, is needed to supply the extra activation energy.
options.C: Both parts are unhelpful. Room temperature would make the slower chloroalkane reaction even slower. And although $\text{C-Cl}$ is more polar, polarity does not explain why harsher conditions are needed.
options.D: Room temperature is too mild for the less reactive chloroalkane. It is true that $\text{C-Cl}$ is shorter than $\text{C-I}$, but shortness alone is not the direct energy reason. The examiner wants strength (bond enthalpy) as the reason for needing reflux.
